explanation: Davis put rivets at the pocket corners of workmen's trousers so they stopped tearing. He could not afford the patent fee, so he teamed up with Strauss, his cloth supplier.

claims.text: In 1873 Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis received a US patent for using copper rivets to strengthen work trousers, the origin of blue jeans.
The Strauss and Davis rivet patent was not for waistcoats, boots or overcoats.
Jacob Davis, a tailor, used rivets to strengthen the pocket corners of workmen's trousers.
Davis could not afford the patent application fee and asked Levi Strauss, who supplied his cloth, to partner with him.
